title: George and Pompy-ompy Pearson
body: George Pearson comes home to find his wife drinking stout in the afternoon. He tells her he will not want tea because there is a special snooker match night at the club. When she replies that there is no tea anyway, he is aggrieved and asks what would have happened if he had wanted some. Mrs Pearson laughs at a man annoyed about not getting a tea he does not even want, and compares it with going to the club bar and complaining that a beer he does not want has not been poured. She then tells him that the men at the club laugh at him behind his back and call him 'Pompy-ompy Pearson' because they think him slow and pompous. Horrified, George appeals to Cyril, who admits in embarrassment that it is true. George leaves the room 'almost as if somebody had hit him over the head'.
